title: DNA extraction and Nanopore library prep from single flies
author: Bernard Y Kim
materials: Per 1 fly, prepare Lysis Master Mix (LMM) Contributed by users : 250 µL, Lysis Buffer 3.13 µL, of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K Solution (20 mg/ml) RNA grade Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #25530-049 (final concentration of 561 μg/mL) 5 µL, of 2 mg/mL final concentration of 0.28% SDS)

Homogenize flies with NEB pestle, working quickly to avoid endogenous nuclease digestion of DNA. Add 200 µL, LMM to the LoBind tube and mix thoroughly using the pestle. Monarch Pestle Set (New England BioLabs, T3000L, https://www.neb.com/products/t3000-monarch-pestle-set#Product%20Information )
Using a 10uL pipette, remove any excess ethanol.
4 µL, of 20 mg/mL RNase A solution Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #R6148 (final concentration of 186 μg/mL)

steps.title: (Optional) Hydration of ethanol-fixed tissue
steps.instruction: Place flies on a sheet of filter paper and briefly dab with a Kimwipe to remove excess ethanol, then transfer the flies to a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: (Optional) Hydration of ethanol-fixed tissue
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL Buffer STE to the tube with the flies. Hydration Buffer (STE) [400mM NaCl 20mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0 30mM EDTA] Contributed by users

steps.title: (Optional) Hydration of ethanol-fixed tissue
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for at least 00:15:00 .

steps.title: Tissue homogenization
steps.instruction: Add 1 fly to a LoBind tube DNA LoBind tubes, 1.5 mL (Tubes, Eppendorf, 022431021, 1.5 mL, https://online-shop.eppendorf.us/US-en/Laboratory-Consumables-44512/Tubes-44515/DNA-LoBind-Tubes-PF-56252.html )

steps.title: Lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate lysis tube at 50 °C for 03:00:00 . Mix the tube with gentle rocking and inversion, until solution appears relatively homogeneous, at 00:30:00 intervals.

steps.title: Spin down phase lock gel tube
steps.instruction: Spin down 1 phase lock gel tube per sample at 15000 x g, °C, for 00:00:30 . Although not essental, phase lock gel tubes help minimize shearing and loss of yield caused by repeated pipetting. Dow Corning High Vacuum Grease is compositionally identical to the light phase lock gel material. We buy the 5.3oz tube from Amazon and squeeze some into a 10mL BD syringe for dispensing. This size of tube/syringe fits well for minimial mess and hassle. Avoid overfilling and air bubbles. Autoclave but be warned this may cause a mess, so wrap the syringe in foil beforehand. About 250 µL of grease is placed into a 2mL LoBind tube to make the homebrew phase lock gel tube. IMPORTANT : If an insufficient amount of grease is applied, the phase lock layer will collapse during the chloroform extraction. Reference: https://bitesizebio.com/18944/diy-phase-separating-gel-clean-and-cheap/ WARNING : If you are using normal tubes in lieu of LoBinds, do not use polystyrene tubes for the phenol-chloroform extraction. They will melt and burst in the centrifuge. Polypropylene tubes do not melt. 5PRIME Phase Lock Gel tube, light, 2mL (Quantabio, 2302820, Light, https://www.quantabio.com/phase-lock-gel )

substeps.instruction: Spin down 1 phase‑lock gel tube per sample at 15000 × g, °C, for 00:00:30
Squeeze grease from a 5.3 oz Dow Corning High Vacuum Grease tube into a 10 mL BD syringe
Avoid overfilling the syringe and prevent air bubbles
Wrap the syringe in foil, then autoclave
Transfer ~250 µL grease into a 2 mL LoBind tube to make home‑brew gel
Ensure sufficient grease (≥250 µL) to avoid layer collapse
Use polypropylene tubes (not polystyrene) for phenol‑chloroform extraction

steps.title: Phenol chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate/lysis solution to the phase lock gel tube by pipetting with a wide-bore tip.

steps.title: Add PCI to phase lock tube
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (about 200 µL ) of Tris-saturated phenol chloroform isoamyl alcohol (PCI) to the phase lock tube. This should be performed inside the fume hood. Phenol Chloroform Isoamyl Alcohol (25:24:1) Tris-saturated (pH 8.0) Fisher Scientific Catalog #BP1752I-400 (CAS: 108-95-2)

substeps.instruction: Add ~200 µL (equal volume) of Tris‑saturated phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1, pH 8.0) (Fisher Scientific catalog #BP1752I‑400, CAS 108‑95‑2) to the phase‑lock tube.
Perform the addition inside a fume hood.

steps.title: Mix sample on rocker
steps.instruction: Mix by placing tubes on a rocker at medium speed for 00:08:00 . Before placing on the rocker, invert by hand until you see the phenol-chloroform and sample as well mixed in the tube. We use a rocking platform, so the tubes are placed on their sides horizontally to maximize the surface area. When solution is well mixed, aqueous (top) layer will be a cloudy milky color.

substeps.instruction: Invert tubes by hand until phenol‑chloroform and sample appear fully mixed
Place tubes on their sides horizontally on the rocker
Set rocker to medium speed and run for 00:08:00
Confirm mixing: aqueous top layer should be a cloudy milky color

steps.title: Phenol chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the phase lock tube at 10000 x g, °C, for 00:08:00 . Phase lock layer should now separate aqueous and organic layers.

steps.title: Phenol chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (usually 200 µL ) of chloroform to the tube. This step should be performed inside the fume hood. Chloroform Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #CX1055-6 (CAS: 67-66-3)

steps.title: Phenol chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the phase lock tube at 15000 x g, °C, for 00:08:00 . Phase lock layer should now separate aqueous and organic layers.

steps.title: Phenol chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Mix by placing tubes on a rocker at medium speed for 00:08:00 .

steps.title: Decant aqueous layer into LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Quickly decant the aqueous (top) layer into a fresh 1.5 mL LoBind tube. Try to perform the decanting step in a few seconds, and don't tap/shake the phase lock tube to get the last drops out. Care must be taken as the chloform significantly weakens the phase lock gel layer. If the phase lock tube is inverted for too long during decanting, the layer will collapse and everything will pour out. It's best to leave a couple of drops behind but avoid the hassle of cleaning this up. IMPORTANT : It is highly recommended to use LoBind tubes in this and subsequent steps. The coating will prevent DNA sticking to the tube. This is helpful for maximizing yield and minimizing shearing. This step should be performed inside the fume hood. DNA LoBind tubes, 1.5 mL (Tubes, Eppendorf, 022431048, 1.5 mL, https://online-shop.eppendorf.us/US-en/Laboratory-Consumables-44512/Tubes-44515/DNA-LoBind-Tubes-PF-56252.html )

substeps.instruction: Quickly decant the aqueous (top) layer into a fresh 1.5 mL LoBind tube.
Complete the decant within a few seconds; do not tap or shake the phase‑lock tube to retrieve the last drops.
Avoid keeping the phase‑lock tube inverted for long, as chloroform weakens the gel and the layer may collapse.
Leave a couple of drops of the aqueous layer behind rather than trying to recover them.
Use DNA LoBind tubes (e.g., Eppendorf 022431048) to prevent DNA adhesion.
Perform the entire step inside the fume hood.

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Chill 100% ethanol on ice and make 500 µL per sample of fresh 70% ethanol using nuclease-free water.

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Add 0.1x volume (typically 20 µL ) of 3M sodium acetate to the extract from Step 19. Gently tap to mix. 3M Sodium Acetate Contributed by users

steps.title: Add ethanol and mix
steps.instruction: Add 2-2.5x volumes (typically 440 µL ) of cold 100% ethanol to the tube, and mix with careful swirling and gentle rocking. DNA should slowly precipitate into a single white stringy clump, and un-precipitated DNA should be visible as shimmering strands at the bottom of the tube that are attached to the white clump. Depending on the size of the fly, DNA precipitation may not be visible. If the extraction tube turns cloudy, it is likely salt precipitation because the solution is too nonpolar and not DNA. Add water dropwise with thorough mixing and the solution should clear up.

substeps.instruction: Add 2–2.5× volume (≈440 µL) cold 100 % ethanol to the tube
Mix by careful swirling and gentle rocking
Add water dropwise with thorough mixing

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 10000 x g, °C, for 00:10:00 .

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: While being careful not to disturb the pellet, pipette off the ethanol. We recommend leaving ~10-15uL of supernatant at the bottom of the tube, especially in cases where the DNA pellet may be invisible.

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet once more: go to step #25 .

steps.title: Air-dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Allow the DNA to air dry right until the moment it becomes translucent (usually 00:02:00 ). Do not over-dry the pellet . Oftentimes the whole DNA pellet will not become translucent but the edges of the pellet will. It is essential to not let the pellet dry out. Especially when working with "invisible pellets," shorten drying time.

substeps.instruction: Air-dry DNA pellet until it becomes translucent (≈2 min)
Do not over‑dry; stop before pellet fully dries
If pellet is invisible, shorten drying time

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend in 30uL of 10 mM Tris-HCL pH 8.0 Contributed by users and incubate at 50 °C for at least 01:00:00 . We recommend 30uL of Tris for resuspension for R10.4.1 sequencing

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Briefly spin down tube to gather any condensation and store at 4 °C .

steps.title: Incubate DNA at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Keep the DNA at 4C for at least, one night depending on previous pellet size. It could be left to resuspend for even 1 week to obtain proper resuspension if need be. Due to sample limitations of working with single flies, there are no shearing steps in this protocol (different from the previous protocol). Instead, take all precautions to protect DNA from shearing.

substeps.instruction: Incubate DNA at 4 °C for ≥1 night (adjust based on pellet size)
If needed, continue incubation up to 1 week for full resuspension
Handle gently; avoid vortexing or vigorous pipetting to prevent shearing

steps.title: Assess sample concentration and quality
steps.instruction: Check sample concentration and quality of 1 µL aliquots using Qubit and Nanodrop. Ideally, this should Qubit at >75 ng/uL and have Nanodrop ratios of 260/280 >1.8 and 260/230 >2.0. If sample is above 150 ng/uL consider diluting with more 10mM tris.

substeps.instruction: Measure 1 µL aliquot on Qubit; record concentration
Measure same aliquot on Nanodrop; record 260/280 and 260/230 ratios
Confirm Qubit >75 ng/µL and Nanodrop ratios 260/280 >1.8, 260/230 >2.0
If concentration >150 ng/µL, dilute with 10 mM Tris

steps.title: Thaw and process NEBNext mixes
steps.instruction: Thaw NEBNext repair and DNA-tailing mixes and buffers from the Nanopore Companion Module. Vortex buffers and flick mixes after thawing. Spin down tubes and keep chilled on ice. NEBNext Companion Module forOxford Nanopore Technologies Ligation Sequencing – 24 rxns New England Biolabs Catalog #E7180S

substeps.instruction: Thaw NEBNext repair and DNA‑tailing mixes and buffers from the Nanopore Companion Module.
Vortex the buffers and flick the mixes after thawing.
Spin down the tubes and keep them chilled on ice.

steps.title: Add reagents and DNA, mix
steps.instruction: Add 1.75 µL of FFPE DNA Repair Buffer, 1.75 µL of End-Prep Reaction Buffer, 1 µL of FFPE DNA Repair Mix, and 1.5 µL of End-Prep Reaction Mix to a PCR tube. Add remaining 24 µL of DNA sample to the PCR tube using a cut-off P200 tip. Mix tube with gentle flicking (or very gentle pipetting with the cut-off P200 tip), and then briefly spin down. To increase efficiency and decrease amount of pipette tips needed, prep PCR tubes with buffers and mixes and add the HMW DNA sample last. We have found no change in yield by halving the standard protocol, even with use of more than one fly. PCR Tubes, 0.2mL, flat cap, natural, PCR Tube; 0.2mL; Natural; w/flat cap; 1000/Pk. Thermo Fisher Catalog #3412 Nuclease-free water or water filtered using a Milli-Q filtering system Ambion Catalog #AM9932

substeps.instruction: Pre‑load PCR tubes with 1.75 µL FFPE DNA Repair Buffer, 1.75 µL End‑Prep Reaction Buffer, 1 µL FFPE DNA Repair Mix, and 1.5 µL End‑Prep Reaction Mix.
Add the remaining 24 µL high‑molecular‑weight DNA sample using a cut‑off P200 tip.
Mix the tube by gentle flicking (or very gentle pipetting with the cut‑off P200 tip).
Briefly spin the tube down.

steps.title: DNA repair and end-prep
steps.instruction: In a thermal cycler, incubate at 20 °C for 01:00:00 then 65 °C for 00:30:00 . After this, sample can be held at 4 °C temporarily until ready to proceed.

steps.title: Prepare ligation master mix
steps.instruction: Thaw AMXF, Quick T4 ligase, LNB, and LFB from the NEBNext Nanopore Companion Module and the Nanopore LSK110 kit. Mix AMXF, Quick T4 ligase, and LFB by flicking. Mix LNB by pipetting. Briefly spin the tubes down and keep chilled on ice. NEBNext Companion Module forOxford Nanopore Technologies Ligation Sequencing – 24 rxns New England Biolabs Catalog #E7180S Ligation sequencing kit 1D Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #SQK-LSK109

substeps.instruction: Thaw AMXF, Quick T4 ligase, LNB, and LFB (from the NEBNext Nanopore Companion Module and Nanopore LSK110 kit) on ice
Mix AMXF, Quick T4 ligase, and LFB by flicking
Mix LNB by pipetting
Briefly spin tubes down
Keep tubes chilled on ice

steps.title: Add DNA sample and reagents to tube
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL prepared DNA sample (the extra 1 µL can be used to Qubit), 2.5 µL AMXF, and 5 µL Quick T4 ligase to a fresh 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube. Gently flick the tube to mix. DNA LoBind Tubes, 1.5 mL Eppendorf Catalog #0030108051 NEBNext Companion Module forOxford Nanopore Technologies Ligation Sequencing – 24 rxns New England Biolabs Catalog #E7180S Ligation sequencing kit 1D Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #SQK-LSK109

substeps.instruction: Add 30 µL prepared DNA sample
Add 2.5 µL AMXF
Add 5 µL Quick T4 ligase
Add extra 1 µL prepared DNA sample to Qubit
Transfer to a fresh 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube
Gently flick the tube to mix

steps.title: Add LNB and mix
steps.instruction: Add 12.5 µL LNB to the sample. Working quickly, mix by gentle pipetting with a wide-bore tip. DNA precipitation is normal, but if the DNA precipitates before you finish mixing it will stick to your pipette tip and you will lose a significant amount of library. Ligation sequencing kit 1D Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #SQK-LSK109 Large-Orifice Pipet Tips 200μL Fisher Scientific Catalog #02-707-134

substeps.instruction: Add 12.5 µL LNB to sample.
Mix quickly by gentle pipetting using a wide‑bore tip.
Note: DNA may precipitate; finish mixing promptly to prevent loss.
Use Ligation sequencing kit 1D (ONT SQK‑LSK109) and 200 µL large‑orifice pipet tips (Fisher #02‑707‑134).

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Incubate the reaction mixture at room temperature for 00:20:00 .

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of AmPure XP beads and mix quickly with wide-bore tip.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for 00:20:00 .

steps.title: Add LFB and tap tube
steps.instruction: Add 95 µL of LFB to the tube. SFB or a 1:1 dilution of PB can be used here. Ligation sequencing kit 1D Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #SQK-LSK109 DO NOT USE ETHANOL TO WASH PREPARED LIBRARY. It will denature the motor protein. Lightly tap the tube to encourage adapter on the beads to come off, but not necessarily for beads to resuspend.

substeps.instruction: Add 95 µL of LFB to the tube (Ligation sequencing kit 1D, Oxford Nanopore Technologies, Catalog #SQK-LSK109).
If desired, substitute SFB or a 1:1 dilution of PB for LFB.
Do NOT use ethanol to wash the prepared library (ethanol denatures the motor protein).
Lightly tap the tube to encourage adapters on the beads to release (no need to fully resuspend beads).

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Being careful not to disturb the pellet, pipette off all the supernatant.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Wash again using 105 µL of LFB. Pipette LFB on to the beads more quickly to get the pellet off the side of the tube. Lightly tap the tube to mix but not fully resuspend.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 21 µL EB for R9.4.1 sequencing or in 30 µL for R10.4.1 sequencing. Elution Buffer (EB) [10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0] Contributed by users

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Incubate library on the heat block at 34 °C for 01:00:00 . Briefly spin down the tube to collect condensation then incubate for at least 48:00:00 before the next step.

steps.title: Quantify library concentration
steps.instruction: Quantify library concentration using 1 µL of the prepared library with Qubit. This step should not be performed unless library concentration is greater than 40 ng/uL. If the concentration is greater than 100ng/uL the library should be diluted to improve size selection performance.

substeps.instruction: Use 1 µL of the prepared library and measure concentration with Qubit.
Perform this only if the library concentration is > 40 ng/µL.
If the measured concentration is > 100 ng/µL, dilute the library to improve size selection performance.

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume ( 20 µL ) of SRE XL buffer to the library and gently pipette mix using a wide-bore tip. Short Read Eliminator (SRE) Circulomics Catalog #SS-100-101-01 Large-Orifice Pipet Tips 200μL Fisher Scientific Catalog #02-707-134

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10000 x g, °C, 30 minutes .

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Pipette off the supernatant, being careful not to disturb the DNA pellet at the bottom of the tube. Similar to previous SRE step, leave 10-15uL of supernatant in the bottom of the tube for the first wash.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 100 µL buffer
steps.instruction: Add 100 uL of LFB, SFB, or 1:1 diluted PB (similar to step 46) to wash the pellet. It does not really matter which one is used. DO NOT USE ETHANOL TO WASH PREPARED LIBRARY. It will denature the motor protein. Ligation sequencing kit 1D Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #SQK-LSK109 DNA Precipitation Buffer (PB) [0.8 M NaCl 9% w/v PEG 8000 10mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0] Contributed by users

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µL of LFB, SFB, or 1:1 diluted PB (as in step 46) to wash the pellet.
Do not use ethanol for the wash; ethanol denatures the motor protein.
If using PB, ensure it contains 0.8 M NaCl, 9 % w/v PEG 8000, and 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0.

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge tube at 10000 x g, Room temperature, for 00:02:00 .

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Being careful not to disturb the pellet, pipette off all the supernatant.

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Repeat wash: go to step #84

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 21 µL EB for R9.4.1 sequencing or in 30 µL for R10.4.1 sequencing. Elution Buffer (EB) [10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0] Contributed by users

steps.title: (Optional) Library size selection with SRE buffer
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube on the heat block at 37 °C for 01:00:00 . Briefly spin down the tube to collect condensation, and incubate at least 48:00:00 at 4 °C before sequencing.

steps.title: Tips for sequencing the library- R9.4.1
steps.instruction: Quantify the concentration of 1 µL library with Qubit. We usually end up with 1000 ng - 2000 ng of total library at this stage.

steps.title: Transfer library to LoBind tube
steps.instruction: With a cut off P200 tip, transfer about 350 ng of prepared library to a fresh 1.5mL LoBind tube. This should not exceed 35 µL in volume. DNA LoBind Tubes, 1.5 mL Eppendorf Catalog #0030108051 To maximize throughput and read length, it is critical to load enough library that flow cell pores will be occupied but not so much that they are oversaturated. The molar concentration of the library is a function of the fragment lengths so it is difficult to say exactly how much library to load. The average library prepared in this manner usually sequences well when 300 ng to 500 ng of DNA is loaded. Note that flow cells need to be flushed and reloaded so we usually aim to have at least 3 library loads.

substeps.instruction: Using a cut‑off P200 tip, transfer ~350 ng (≤35 µL) of prepared library into a fresh 1.5 mL LoBind tube (Eppendorf catalog #0030108051).

steps.title: Add SQB and FB to tube
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of SQB to the tube. Then, add FB from the marked tube (the one that we are not going to prepare the priming mix with) to a final volume of 70 µL . For example, if 10 µL of 35 ng/μL library was transferred in step 77, add 10 µL of SQB and 50 µL FB to the tube. Ligation sequencing kit 1D Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #SQK-LSK109 Flow Cell Priming Kit (EXP-FLP002) Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #EXP-FLP002

substeps.instruction: Add SQB volume equal to the library volume already in the tube.
Add FB from the marked tube (not used for priming mix) until total volume reaches 70 µL.
Example: if 10 µL of 35 ng/µL library was transferred, add 10 µL SQB and 50 µL FB.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw 1 tube SQB (SQK-LSK109), 2 tubes FB (EXP-FLP002), and 1 tube FLT (EXP-FLP002). Mix SQB and FB by flicking. Mix FLT with a pipette. Keep reagents on ice until ready to sequence. We recommend marking one tube of FB to use as dilution buffer for subsequent runs. Only one tube should be used to prepare the priming mix. The FB must be from the EXP-FLP002 kit. This will not work with version 1 of the kit.

substeps.instruction: Thaw 1 SQB tube (SQK-LSK109), 2 FB tubes (EXP-FLP002), and 1 FLT tube (EXP-FLP002).
Flick‑mix SQB with FB.
Pipette‑mix FLT.
Keep all reagents on ice until sequencing.
Mark one FB tube as dilution buffer for future runs.
Use only one tube to prepare the priming mix.
Ensure FB is from the EXP-FLP002 kit.
Do not use kit version 1.

steps.title: Prime flow cell and load library
steps.instruction: Follow the official instructions to prime the flow cell, then add the prepared library to the flow cell. When loading the library, be sure to use a wide-bore pipette tip. Gently pipette mix the library before loading to ensure even distribution of the library across the flow cell membrane. Large-Orifice Pipet Tips 200μL Fisher Scientific Catalog #02-707-134

substeps.instruction: Follow official instructions to prime the flow cell
Use a wide‑bore (Large‑Orifice) 200 µL pipette tip (Fisher Scientific Catalog #02-707-134) to add the prepared library to the flow cell
Gently pipette‑mix the library before loading to ensure even distribution across the flow cell membrane

steps.title: Flush flow cell
steps.instruction: Over the course of a sequencing run, pores will get clogged and become inactive. It is essential to flush the flow cell at 10-14 hour intervals to make these pores available again. We recommend Nanopore's Flow Cell Wash Kit (EXP-WSH003). Flowcell Wash Kit Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #EXP-WSH003

substeps.instruction: Flush the flow cell every 10–14 h
Use Nanopore Flow Cell Wash Kit (EXP‑WSH003)

steps.title: Tissue homogenization
steps.instruction: Prepare Lysis Buffer Contributed by users , 10% SDS Contributed by users , 3M Sodium Acetate Contributed by users , and Lysis Master Mix (LMM) Contributed by users

steps.title: Tissue homogenization
steps.instruction: For Lysis Buffer Contributed by users : 5 mL Molarity (M), Tris-HCl pH 8.0 2 mL 0.5 Molarity (M), EDTA 0.292 g, NaCl 43 mL, DI H20

steps.title: Tissue homogenization
steps.instruction: For 10% SDS Contributed by users : 5 g SDS 50 mL Distilled H20

steps.title: Tissue homogenization
steps.instruction: For 3M Sodium Acetate Contributed by users : 2.461 g, NaOAc 10 mL, DI H20

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Add 175 µL of 70% ethanol.

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Spin at 12500 x g, , for 00:05:00 .

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Being careful not to disturb the DNA pellet, remove the ethanol.

steps.title: DNA precipitation, wash, and resuspension
steps.instruction: Spin at 12500 rcf, , for 00:01:00 .

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Prepare 250 µL of 80% ethanol per sample.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Transfer sample from PCR tube to a LoBind tube using a cut-off P200 tip.

steps.title: Add beads and mix
steps.instruction: Add equal volume of AmPure XP beads (normally 30 µL ) to the sample. Immediately use a P200 wide bore tip to mix 5x. This step must be performed quickly; otherwise, DNA will precipitate onto pipette tip and will result in sample loss. If needed, briefly spin down to ensure there are no bubbles or any sample on the wall of the LoBind tube. Agencourt AmPure XP beads Contributed by users Catalog #A63880

substeps.instruction: Add equal volume of AMPure XP beads (≈30 µL) to the sample.
Immediately mix 5 times using a P200 wide‑bore tip (perform quickly).
If needed, briefly spin down the LoBind tube to eliminate bubbles and any sample adhering to the wall.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Incubate at room temperature for 00:20:00 .

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Place the LoBind tube on a magnetic rack and wait until solution is clear and the beads are pelleted.

steps.title: Remove supernatant from LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant by placing pipette tip on the wall of the LoBind tube opposite of the beads. Pipette very slowly to ensure no DNA is pulled off. If DNA is pulled off, add supernatant back to tube and wait for solution to clear. Then try again.

substeps.instruction: Place pipette tip against the tube wall opposite the beads.
Pipette very slowly to remove the supernatant.
If DNA is pulled off, add the supernatant back to the tube.
Wait for the solution to clear.
Repeat the removal step.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Wash by adding 100 µL of 80% ethanol (enough to cover the beads on the wall of the LoBind tube). Work quickly to add the 80% ethanol at this step to avoid the beads drying out.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Remove and discard ethanol.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Wash again by adding 115 µL of 70% ethanol.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Remove and discard ethanol. Briefly spin and use a P10 pipette to remove any remaining excess of ethanol.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Resuspend sample in 32 µL of nuclease-free water.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet on heat block
steps.instruction: Place tube on heat block at 50 °C until the pellet has dissolved. This step can take a long time. If there is concern about the DNA not resuspending off the beads, the tube can be stored at 4 °C overnight and then the sample removed from the beads the following morning.

substeps.instruction: Place tube on heat block set to 50 °C.
Incubate until the pellet fully dissolves (may take a long time).
If DNA resuspension is uncertain, store tube at 4 °C overnight.
Next morning, remove the sample from the beads.

steps.title: Bead Clean Up
steps.instruction: Place LoBind tube on magnet rack until solution is clear.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Using a cut off P200 tip, remove the supernatant containing the aqueous DNA. Qubit 1 µL of sample to ensure DNA concentration before proceeding to next step. This is a safe stopping point. Sample can be stored at 4 °C .

substeps.instruction: Using a cut‑off P200 tip, remove the supernatant containing the aqueous DNA.
Take 1 µL of the sample and measure DNA concentration with a Qubit fluorometer.
Store the remaining sample at 4 °C as a safe stopping point.

steps.title: Add SRE XL buffer and mix
steps.instruction: If sample concentration is greater than 40ng/uL, add equal volume (usually around 30 µL ) SRE XL buffer. Using a wide-bore P200 tip, quickly but gently mix the tube. The precipitation buffer described here can be used in place of the SRE buffer but is not as effective at removing small DNA fragments as SRE. steps.title: Short Read Elimination 1
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 10000 x g, °C, for 00:30:00 or until DNA has pelleted and solution is no longer viscous. Meanwhile, prepare 500 µL fresh 70% ethanol with nuclease-free water.

steps.title: Remove supernatant, leave residual
steps.instruction: Pipette off the supernatant, taking care not to disturb the DNA pellet. We have increased our yield by leaving 10-15 uL of supernatant in the bottom of the tube going into the first wash. This is particularly important if the pellet is invisible.

substeps.instruction: Pipette off supernatant, avoiding disturbance of DNA pellet
Leave 10–15 µL supernatant in tube bottom for first wash

steps.title: Short Read Elimination 1
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of 70% ethanol. Pipette slowly, with the tip touching the front wall of the tube, so that the pellet is not disturbed.

steps.title: Short Read Elimination 1
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10000 x g, °C, for 00:02:00 .

steps.title: Short Read Elimination 1
steps.instruction: Pipette off the supernatant, taking care not to disturb the DNA pellet. Make sure all the supernatant is removed and only the pellet remains.

steps.title: Short Read Elimination 1
steps.instruction: Repeat wash: go to step #39 The second centrifuge (step 43) can be shorter, ~1 minute.

steps.title: Short Read Elimination 1
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 25 µL EB. Elution Buffer (EB) [10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0] Contributed by users

steps.title: Incubate tube and spin
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube on the heat block at 50 °C for at least 01:00:00 . Briefly spin down the tube to collect condensation. Incubate for at least 48:00:00 at 4 °C . Before proceeding to the next stage, we recommend 1 µL Qubit to ensure there is still DNA.

Briefly spin down tube to collect condensation.
Incubate tube at 4 °C for ≥ 48 h.
Take 1 µL for Qubit assay to check DNA.

steps.title: Short Read Elimination 1
steps.instruction: Briefly spin sample and use a P10 to remove any remaining ethanol.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Place tubes on magnetic and wait for solution to clear.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: On the magnet, use a cut-off P200 tip to pull the supernatant off the beads very slowly, then dispense the supernatant back onto the bead pellet slowly. Let the sample sit on the magnet for a few minutes.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Pipette off supernatant with a normal pipette tip, pipetting from the front of the tube away from the pellet.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: While on magnet remove LFB. Briefly spin and use a P10 pipette to remove any remaining excess of LFB.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: Place sample on magnet wait until solution is clear. Use a cut off P200 tip to remove sample from beads and place in a new 1.5mL Lo Bind tube.

steps.title: Tips for sequencing the library-R10.4.1
steps.instruction: Thaw 1 tube SB (LSK110), 1 tube LIS, 1 tube of FCF per sample, and 1 tube FCT. Mix SQB and FB by flicking.

steps.title: Tips for sequencing the library-R10.4.1
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL FCT to FCF and pipette 10x to ensure thorough mixing We recommend marking the top of the FCF tube after FCT has been added.

steps.title: Tips for sequencing the library-R10.4.1
steps.instruction: Follow the official instructions to prime the flow cell.

steps.title: Prepare library while priming
steps.instruction: While the flow cell is priming, prepare the library by adding 70uL of LIS, 30uL library (LIS and library should total to 100uL), and 100uL SB. Lightly tap to mix until swirls disappear but wait to pipette mix until just before loading.

substeps.instruction: Add 70 µL LIS to the tube.
Add 30 µL library (ensure LIS + library = 100 µL total).
Add 100 µL SB.
Lightly tap the tube until swirls disappear.
Do NOT pipette‑mix now; perform pipette mixing only just before loading.

steps.title: Tips for sequencing the library-R10.4.1
steps.instruction: Pipette mix prepared library 2x times and then following official instructions to load the flow cell.

steps.title: Flush flow cell
steps.instruction: Over the course of a sequencing run, pores will get clogged and become inactive. It is essential to flush the flow cell at 10-14 hour intervals to make these pores available again. We recommend Nanopore's Flow Cell Wash Kit (EXP-WSH00). Flowcell Wash Kit Oxford Nanopore Technologies Catalog #EXP-WSH003

substeps.instruction: Prepare Nanopore Flow Cell Wash Kit (catalog EXP-WSH00 and EXP-WSH003)
Flush the flow cell every 10–14 hours using the kit
